question.worked_solution:
Notice that we can rewrite the given sum as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}-\frac{(2/3)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(2/3)^{3}}{3}+⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(2/3)^{n}}{n}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x) = \ln(1+x).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x) & =x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x={\color{blue}\dfrac{2}{3}}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+\frac{2}{3}) & =\frac{2}{3}-\frac{(2/3)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(2/3)^{3}}{3}+⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(2/3)^{n}}{n}+⋯ \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{5}{3}) & =\frac{2}{3}-\frac{(2/3)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(2/3)^{3}}{3}+⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(2/3)^{n}}{n}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\ln\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right).$
